children: The broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices and scaled to fresh high during the week, with Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices gaining around 0.5% each, even as the Nifty 50 and Sensex extended their losing streak to the third week.
For the week, the BSE Sensex declined 276.32 points, or 0.35%, to 77,264.51, while the Nifty 50 fell 76.35 points, or 0.31%, to 24,175.65.

The Nifty Midcap 100 index rose 0.5% to hit a fresh all-time high of 64,450.90, led by gains in Steel Authority of India, Glenmark Pharma, LIC Housing Finance and Laurus Labs. On the other hand, Rail Vikas Nigam, Federal Bank, IDFC First Bank, Coromandel International and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company were among the key laggards

The Nifty Smallcap 100 index also gained 0.5% to touch a record high of 20,143.55, supported by double-digit gains in Capri Global Capital, IDBI Bank, IFCI and Ather Energy. Meanwhile, BLS International Services, Aegis Logistics, Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals, CreditAccess Grameen, Hindustan Copper and Tenneco Clean Air India declined between 6% and 12% during the week

The sectoral performance was mixed, with Nifty Metal, IT, Pharma and Healthcare indices rising more than 2% each, while the Nifty Capital Markets index gained 1.5%. On the other hand, Nifty FMCG, Infrastructure and Oil & Gas indices declined 1% each, while Nifty Auto and Defence indices slipped nearly 1% each.

"In the last week, the benchmark indices witnessed range-bound activity after a roller coaster ride. The Nifty ended 0.31 percent lower, while the Sensex declined by 310 points. Among sectors, Pharma and Healthcare indices gained over 1.5 percent, whereas the FMCG index lost the most, shedding 1.95 percent," said Amol Athawale, VP Technical Research, Kotak Securities.

"Technically, on daily charts, it has formed a bearish candle, and on the higher side, it is consistently facing resistance near the 20-day SMA (Simple Moving Average) or the 24,350/77900 zone, which is largely negative."

"We are of the view that the short-term market texture is weak, but a fresh selloff is possible only if the 24,100/77100 level is broken. If that happens, the market could slip to 24000-23,800/76800-76200. On the flip side, the 50-day SMA or 24,200/77500 would act as an immediate resistance zone for traders. If the index manages to trade above this level, it could retest the 20-day SMA at 24,350/77900. Further upside may also continue, potentially lifting the index to 24,500/78400."
"For Bank Nifty, the 50- and 20-day SMAs or 57,700 would serve as immediate reference points for traders. As long as it remains below these levels, weak sentiment is likely to persist."

"Below the same, the chances of hitting 56,800-56,500 increase. Conversely, a move above 57,700 could lead to a bounce back toward 58,000-58,500. The current market texture is non-directional; hence, level-based trading would be the ideal strategy for short-term traders," he added.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net sellers for the second consecutive week, offloading equities worth ₹20,260 crore during the week. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to provide support to the market, investing ₹19,309.93 crore in equities over the week.
The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies declined by a little over Rs 1 lakh crore during the week.
Where is market headed?
Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities.
The 24000–23970 zone is expected to act as a crucial support area for the index. A decisive breach below 23970 could trigger further weakness, paving the way for a correction towards 23820.

On the upside, the 24300–24330 zone is likely to act as an immediate resistance hurdle. A sustained move above this zone would be required to improve the near-term outlook and open the door for further upside.
Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities

After moving below, the higher support of ascending trend line at 24150 levels on Thursday, Nifty was not able to show sharp follow-through weakness on Friday. This is positive indication and such false downside breakouts more often results in sharp upsides.

The underlying trend of Nifty remains range bound (24400-24000) with positive bias. Any sustainable bounceback from near the lower range could open a sizable bounce towards 24300-24400 levels in the near term. Important supports for trend reversal is placed at 24000.
Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities

Nifty moved back into the rising channel following a volatile session. However, the trend remains far from bullish, as the index continues to trade below the 50EMA. Overall, a lack of momentum prevailed, with the index remaining confined within a narrow range.

On the upside, the 24,200 level may continue to act as an immediate resistance. As long as the index remains below 24,200, the broader sentiment is likely to stay weak, with a possibility of a decline towards 23,900 in the near term.
A fall below 23,900 could trigger further correction. On the other hand, a decisive move above 24,200 may lead to an improvement in market sentiment and might strengthen the near-term trend.

title: Mid, smallcaps outperform benchmarks; hit fresh all-time highs
